step1_analysis.description: A differential pair (XM1, XM2) sharing a tail current node with an auxiliary differential pair (XM3, XM4). The auxiliary pair is used to inject an offset current into the output nodes to cancel input-referred offset voltage, commonly used in high-speed optical receivers.

paper_reference.title: A 28Gb/s 1pJ/b Shared-Inductor Optical Receiver with 56% Chip-Area Reduction in 28nm CMOS

Differential_Gain.description: Low-frequency differential voltage gain of the main pair.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a 1mA tail current and 1kOhm load resistors: gm = sqrt(2 * un*Cox * (W/L) * Id) = sqrt(2 * 270uA/V^2 * 10 * 0.25mA) = 1.16mS. Gain = gm * RL = 1.16mS * 1kOhm = 1.16 V/V = 1.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The gain depends heavily on the chosen load resistor and tail current. With 1kOhm and 1mA tail current, gain is around 4.3 dB for a single stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = 1 / (2 * pi * RL * Cout). Cout approx 20fF. BW = 1 / (2 * pi * 1k * 20fF) = 8 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Without the shared inductive peaking mentioned in the paper's title, the bandwidth is strictly limited by the RC time constant of the load resistor and parasitic capacitances.

Power_Consumption.description: Total power consumed by the stage.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the tail current source added in the testbench to bias the differential pairs.

Offset_Tuning_Range.description: Maximum differential output voltage shift achievable by the offset pair.

sky130_expected.reasoning: If the offset pair completely steers the tail current, the output differential voltage can shift by up to I_tail * RL.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure differential gain, bandwidth, power consumption, and offset tuning range.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Differential Amplifier with Offset Cancellation
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 VOUTn VINp TAIL GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VOUTp VINn TAIL GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VOUTn VOFFSETp TAIL GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VOUTp VOFFSETn TAIL GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}

* Power supply and load resistors
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
RL1 VDD VOUTn 1k
RL2 VDD VOUTp 1k

* Tail current source
ITAIL TAIL 0 1m

* Inputs for AC and OP
* AC magnitude is set to 0.5 and -0.5 to provide a 1V differential AC input
VVINp VINp 0 DC 0.9 AC 0.5
VVINn VINn 0 DC 0.9 AC -0.5
VVOFFSETp VOFFSETp 0 DC 0.9
VVOFFSETn VOFFSETn 0 DC 0.9

.control
* 1. Operating Point & Power
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 100 1Meg 100G
let vout_diff = v(VOUTn) - v(VOUTp)
let gain_mag = mag(vout_diff)
let gain_db = 20*log10(gain_mag)
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=1Meg
let gain_3db = dc_gain - 3
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=gain_3db fall=1
print dc_gain bw_3db

* 3. DC Analysis for Offset Tuning Range
dc VVOFFSETp 0.0 1.8 0.01
let vout_diff_dc = v(VOUTn) - v(VOUTp)
meas dc max_offset max vout_diff_dc
meas dc min_offset min vout_diff_dc
let offset_range = max_offset - min_offset
print offset_range

quit
.endc
.end
